summary: 1938 South Carolina Forestry Commission tower near Bonneau, Berkeley County; sold to Billy McIntosh and re-erected on private land in Sumter County; no public access described.

facts.design: 100' Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with 7'x7' steel cab
facts.agency: Built for the South Carolina Forestry Commission; owned by Billy McIntosh per NHLR

access.note: Privately owned by Billy McIntosh; the sources describe hunting use by the owner and his guests, but no public access

events.note: Built for the SC Forestry Commission and erected near Bonneau, Berkeley County
SC Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993 (system-wide; not specific to this tower)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. The Register says the late 1990s, Forest Lookouts gives 199?? and the magazine says the early 2000s. The story reports both and does not choose one.
Not resolved. The Register gives 100 feet for this tower. The magazine says two of McIntosh's four towers stand at their original 110 feet, but does not identify which tower is which.

notes_for_editor: Design, original owner and 1938 build are well supported. The McIntosh purchase year conflicts across sources (late 1990s vs 199?? vs early 2000s) and is left open. The Register's 100 ft height versus the magazine's unassigned 110 ft towers is also unresolved. No staffing names, notable fires, or public-access statement were found. The magazine copy we read is dated June 2018. The 2013 registration date is from the Register.
